clusters.name: Cluster B / Core BPD Symptoms
items: Frantic efforts to avoid abandonment (DSM p.752)
Unstable and intense interpersonal relationships with splitting (DSM p.752)
Identity disturbance (DSM p.752)
Impulsivity in >=2 self-damaging areas (DSM p.752)
Recurrent suicidal behavior, threats, or NSSI (DSM p.753)
Affective instability due to marked mood reactivity (DSM p.753)
Chronic feelings of emptiness (DSM p.753)
Inappropriate, intense anger or control difficulties (DSM p.753)
Transient stress-related paranoid ideation or severe dissociation (DSM p.753)

criteria.thresholds: >=5/9 symptoms, duration >=1 year in adolescents under 18 (DSM p.735, 755)
subtypes: DSM-5-TR Section III Alternative Model: Moderate or greater impairment in personality functioning (Identity, Self-Direction, Empathy, Intimacy) + >=4/7 pathological traits (DSM p.886-887)

epidemiology.prevalence: 1.4%-5.9% general population (median 2.7%) (DSM p.755); 6% primary care, 10% outpatient, 20% inpatient (DSM p.755)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: 3:1 F:M in clinical settings; 1:1 F:M in community samples (DSM p.755-756)
epidemiology.heritability: 5x higher prevalence among first-degree biological relatives (DSM p.755-756)
epidemiology.prognosis: ~6% lifetime suicide mortality (DSM p.756); high rates of stable remission (1-8 years) with impulsivity improving faster than affective symptoms (DSM p.755)

etiology.genetic: 5x increased risk in 1st-degree relatives (DSM p.755-756); BDNF epigenetic alterations from early trauma (StahlNeuro p.147-149)
etiology.neurobiology: Frontolimbic Top-Down failure (VMPFC/OFC -> Amygdala) (StahlNeuro p.453); Ventral Striatal loop in impulsivity (StahlNeuro p.538-540); low 5-HIAA/serotonin dysfunction (Dulcan p.584); reduced plasma oxytocin (Dulcan p.524)
etiology.environmental: Linehan Biosocial Model: temperament x invalidating environment (Synopsis ch.19); high rates of childhood sexual/physical abuse and neglect (DSM p.755, Dulcan p.526)

first_line: DBT / DBT-A (Dialectical Behavior Therapy for Adolescents) (Dulcan p.558)
second_line: Targeted Pharmacotherapy for symptom domains (Dulcan p.557, StahlKids p.138)
key_side_effects: FDA Black Box Warning for suicidality with SSRIs in adolescents (StahlKids p.219)
TEAS (Treatment-Emergent Activation Syndrome) with SSRIs (StahlKids p.219)
Disinhibition with Benzodiazepines leading to worsening anger/NSSI (Synopsis ch.19)
treatment.monitoring: Safety Planning & Means Restriction (Dulcan p.557); C-SSRS for suicide risk (Dulcan p.555); metabolic monitoring for SGAs (StahlKids p.36, 412)

items: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) (Dulcan p.555)
DSM-5 Level 1 Cross-Cutting Symptom Measure (DSM p.843-845)
Personality Inventory for DSM-5 (PID-5) (DSM p.894)
Level of Personality Functioning Scale (LPFS) (DSM p.882, 895)
Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) Dysregulated Phenotype (Dulcan p.62, 86)
K-SADS-PL (Kiddie-SADS) (Dulcan p.75, 255)
key_numbers: 1 year minimum duration for under 18 (DSM p.735, 755)
4/7 pathological personality traits in Section III (DSM p.886-887)
4 modes of DBT (Individual, Group, Phone, Consultation Team) (Synopsis ch.19)

items: Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder (DMDD) (DSM p.178-179, Dulcan p.268)
Pediatric Bipolar Disorder (BD I/II) (DSM p.140, 150, 756, Dulcan p.289)
ADHD / Conduct Disorder (CD) (DSM p.75, 526, Dulcan p.199)
PTSD / Complex PTSD (DSM p.301-303, Dulcan p.352)
Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID) (DSM p.331)
Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) / Frontal Lobe Damage (DSM p.776)
Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (DSM p.776)
PANS / PANDAS and Autoimmune Encephalopathy (Dulcan p.379, 407)
key_numbers: DMDD onset age must be before 10 years, diagnosed between ages 6-18 (DSM p.178)
Bipolar hypomania requires >=4 consecutive days, mania >=1 week (DSM p.140)

items: Marked reactivity of mood to interpersonal stressors (DSM p.753-754)
Episodic dysphoria, panic, anxiety, or intense anger (DSM p.754)
Top-Down prefrontal control failure over hyper-reactive amygdala (StahlNeuro p.453)
Central serotonergic dysfunction / low CSF 5-HIAA (Dulcan p.584)
key_numbers: Mood swings typically last a few hours and rarely more than 2 days (DSM p.754)

items: Frantic efforts to avoid real or imagined abandonment (DSM p.752-753)
Splitting - alternating between extreme idealization and devaluation (DSM p.752, Synopsis ch.19)
Projective Identification - 3-step defense mechanism (Synopsis ch.19)
Separation Insecurity trait in Section III (DSM p.887)
Low plasma oxytocin levels linked to attachment dysregulation (Dulcan p.524)
key_numbers: 3-step process in Projective Identification (Projection, Pressure, Identification) (Synopsis ch.19)

items: Markedly and persistently unstable self-image or sense of self (DSM p.752-753)
Identity Diffusion - lack of coherent integrated self-concept (Synopsis ch.19)
Feeling bad, evil, or non-existent in absence of relationships (DSM p.753)
Chronic feelings of emptiness ('Empty Self') (DSM p.754)
Transient stress-related dissociation (depersonalization/derealization) (DSM p.754)
Differentiated from normative adolescent Identity Problem (DSM p.757)
key_numbers: 1 year minimum duration needed for adolescent diagnosis (DSM p.735, 755)

items: Impulsivity in at least 2 self-damaging areas (spending, sex, substance abuse, reckless driving, binge eating) (DSM p.752-753)
Recurrent suicidal behavior, threats, gestures, or NSSI (DSM p.753)
NSSI serves negative reinforcement (affect regulation / grounding) (DSM p.754, Dulcan p.597)
Ventral Striatal loop dysregulation (Accumbens <-> Thalamus <-> VMPFC/ACC) (StahlNeuro p.538-540)
Aripiprazole, Risperidone, or Lithium for impulsive aggression (StahlKids p.36, 291, 412)
key_numbers: 2 self-damaging areas required for criterion 4 (DSM p.752)
~6% lifetime suicide mortality rate in BPD (DSM p.756)
5 days or more of self-injury per year proposed for NSSI Disorder (DSM p.923)

high_yield: In adolescents under 18, BPD criteria must be present continuously for at least 1 year (DSM p.735, 755).
BPD mood reactivity lasts hours to max 2 days vs. Bipolar episodes lasting days to weeks with decreased need for sleep (DSM p.140, 756).
DMDD occurs in ages 6-18 with onset <10, lacking BPD core identity disturbance, abandonment panic, and splitting (DSM p.178-179).
Lifetime suicide mortality in BPD is ~6%, with impulsive symptoms remitting faster than affective symptoms over time (DSM p.755-756).
DBT-A and MBT-A are first-line evidence-based psychotherapies; pharmacotherapy is off-label and symptom-targeted only (Dulcan p.558, StahlKids p.138).
Benzodiazepines are strictly avoided in BPD due to severe disinhibition worsening rage outbursts and NSSI (Synopsis ch.19).
Impulsivity is driven by Ventral Striatal loop dysfunction (Accumbens <-> VMPFC/ACC) and central serotonin deficit (StahlNeuro p.538, Dulcan p.584).
